  Query and explore study records, samples, runs, harmonized attributes,
  publications, and read-derived quality metrics.
output:
  rmarkdown::html_document:
    self_contained: true
    mathjax: null
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
seqout::SeqoutDefault(NULL)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

`SeqoutGet()` gets the dataset metadata for an archive accession. It also gets the related records from other archives.

```{r setup}
library(seqout)

d <- SeqoutGet("GSE168652")
d
```

Each field loads when you first read it. The client keeps the field in a cache for the reads that follow:

```{r fields}
names(d)
```

| Field | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| `meta` | Study-level metadata: title, abstract, design description, submission dates, and files. |
| `samples` | One row for each sample. |
| `experiments` | Library preparation details, one row for each experiment. |
| `runs` | Runs and their download URLs. |
| `supplementary` | Processed supplementary files for the study and its samples. |
| `bams` | Alignment files that the authors submitted. |
| `pubs` | Publications linked to the dataset. |
| `links` | Accession mappings for the same dataset in other archives. |
| `enriched` | Harmonized sample attributes that `seqout.org` generates. |
| `detail` | The record of the accession, if you call `SeqoutGet()` with a sample or run accession. |
| `kind`, `project`, `geo`, `sra` | The type of the source accession and the mapped parent accessions. |

## Study-level metadata

```{r meta-names}
names(d$meta)
```

```{r meta}
d$meta$title
d$meta$overall_design
c(published = d$meta$published_at, organisms = d$meta$organisms)
```

## Samples, experiments, and runs

`samples` has one row for each sample. Each submitter attribute has its own column:

```{r samples}
d$samples
```

```{r experiments}
d$experiments[, c("accession", "library_strategy", "library_layout", "instrument_model")]
```

```{r runs}
d$runs[, c("run_accession", "experiment_accession", "ncbi_sra_url_aws")]
```

An archive does not always supply each run in each format. Thus, some columns can contain `NA`. This study has no ENA FASTQ files, thus `fastq_ftp` is empty:

```{r runs-fastq}
d$runs[, c("run_accession", "fastq_ftp", "ncbi_sra_normalized_bytes")]
```

To select a format, refer to [Downloads](downloads.html).

## Cross-archive accession mapping

Authors frequently put the same study in more than one archive. `links` gives each resolved accession:

```{r links}
d$links
```

`SeqoutGet()` gives the same dataset for each of these accessions.

To follow one specific link, use one of these four functions. Each function moves one hop and gives one accession. If there is no link, the function gives `NA`:

```{r resolve}
ResolveStudy("SRR13927092") # run, experiment or sample -> its study
GSMSeries("GSM5155196") # GEO sample -> its series
LinkedStudy("GSE168652") # series -> the sequencing study holding its runs
LinkedGEO("SRP310948") # sequencing study -> the series holding its processed files
```

`AccessionKind()` finds the type of an accession. It does not send an API request:

```{r kind}
AccessionKind("GSE168652")
AccessionKind("SRR12012336")
AccessionKind("E-MTAB-11467")
```

## Harmonized sample metadata

`seqout.org` maps free-text sample attributes to a shared vocabulary of tissues, diseases, cell types, assays, and developmental stages.

The `enriched` field contains these harmonized attributes:

```{r enriched}
d$enriched[, c("sample", "tissue", "disease", "assay", "assay_category")]
```

Each harmonized field has an ontology identifier (CURIE) from an ontology such as UBERON, MONDO, or CL. With these identifiers, you can group and compare samples across studies:

```{r enriched-ids}
d$enriched[, c("sample", "disease_ontology_id", "disease_ontology_name")]
```

To make cohorts across studies from these standardized fields, refer to [Search](search.html).

## Mapped publications

`pubs` gives the linked publications with their journal names and citation counts:

```{r pubs}
d$pubs[, c("pmid", "title", "journal", "citation_count")]
```

For publication and author lookups with `Paper()` and `Author()`, refer to [Search](search.html).

## Retrieve summaries for multiple accessions

`Summaries()` gets short records for more than one project in one API call:

```{r summaries}
Summaries(c("GSE168652", "GSE151530", "SRP267291"))
```

## Read-derived quality metrics

`seqout` also screens the raw reads, in addition to the metadata from the submitter. The screen makes sure that the metadata is correct and finds the composition of each sample.

### Single-cell metadata

`ProjectSingleCell()` gives read-derived single-cell metrics. These metrics include cell and gene counts, predicted assay categories, and sex verification verdicts:

```{r single-cell}
sc <- ProjectSingleCell("GSE168652")
sc[, c("sample_accession", "cells", "genes", "assay_display", "sex_verdict")]
```

> [!NOTE]
> The `cells` field gives the number of columns in the raw expression matrix. For an unfiltered 10x Genomics dataset, this number includes all detected barcodes. Thus, it is an upper bound for the number of final cells.

To find only if a study is single-cell, and the evidence for that result, call `ProjectSingleCellStatus()`.

`ProjectSingleCellSummary()` combines the per-sample metrics into one study-level row:

```{r single-cell-study}
status <- ProjectSingleCellStatus("GSE168652")
status[, c("accession", "single_cell_status", "n_independent_evidence", "has_matrix")]

s <- ProjectSingleCellSummary("GSE168652")
s[, c("study_accession", "study_cells", "n_samples_reported", "any_unfiltered")]
```

### Long-read chemistry

For PacBio and Oxford Nanopore studies, `ProjectLongreadChemistry()` lists each long-read run, with the instrument and chemistry that sequenced the run:

```{r longread-chemistry}
LongreadProjects(technology = "PacBio", sort = "n_runs", order = "asc", limit = 1)$study_accession |>
  ProjectLongreadChemistry()
```

### Microbial screening

`seqout` also screens the reads for microbial sequences. `has_viral_reads` and `has_bacterial_reads` flag microbial content that passed the quality gates of the screen. A value of `NA` shows that `seqout` did not screen the sample.

```{r flags}
sc[, c("sample_accession", "has_viral_reads", "hpv_top_type", "n_flags")]
```

`SampleMicrobes()` lists each microbial detection. The list also contains the detections below the quality gate:

```{r microbes}
m <- SampleMicrobes("GSM5155196", kind = "viral")
m[, c("organism", "n_unitigs", "max_breadth_frac")]
```

`max_breadth_frac` is the fraction of the reference genome that the detection covers. If a detection is below the report gate, `has_viral_reads` stays `FALSE`.

`validated_only = TRUE` keeps only the detections that pass the quality gate. By default, the function removes common spike-ins, negative controls, and background contaminants. To keep them, set `include_background = TRUE`.

## Retrieve sample or run details

If you call `SeqoutGet()` with a sample (GSM) or run (SRR) accession, the function puts that record in `detail`:

```{r detail}
s <- SeqoutGet("GSM5155196")
s$kind
s$detail[, c("accession", "title", "tissue", "platform_ref")]
```

The other fields contain the data for the parent study:

```{r detail-project}
s$project
nrow(s$samples)
```
